tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	This is a take home coding assignment for https://catalyst.app/.
2	
3	Catalyst is the agent layer for finance. We turn natural language — a thesis, strategy, hedge, or trading idea — into live execution across any market, venue, or asset class from prediction markets to commodities to tokens to private markets. It is a seed stage company with investments from Sequoia, Jump Trading, and Lux Capital.
4	
5	Here are more details about Catalyst: https://coastalhq.co/scoop/e3a34548-1964-4b30-96ea-52801a558dd2
6	
7	The goal of the project is to create a functional protoype of the concept behind Catalyst as a company. The full brief I was provided for this is located at ./ASSIGNMENT.md
8	
9	## Map
10	
11	| Where | What |
12	|-------|------|
13	| `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` | The compressed seed: decisions, requirements, invariants, anti-patterns, roadmap as PR stacks |
14	| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | The technical counterpart: layers, data flow, where each invariant is enforced, runtime, testing. Living; marks each section built or planned |
15	| `docs/adr/` | Numbered decision records (MADR format: context, options, decision, consequences); `template.md`; `README.md` index. Higher number supersedes |
16	| `spec/` | The spec as a book: one directory per idea (`graph/`, `multiverse/`, `thesis/`, `generation/`, `workbench/`, `probes/`), each with a landing page; `vocabulary.md` is the shared language |
17	| `docs/research/` | Four independent research reports (2026-09-16) that fed the PRD; inputs, not decisions |
18	| `plans/` | **Local only, git-ignored.** Agent-to-agent handoffs, working notes, orchestration. Start at `plans/README.md`. Nothing here is a source of truth — anything durable moves into a root document, a decision record, or the spec |
19	| `docs/initial-brainstorming.md` | Kent's raw notes; the origin of trigger/sustain links and refinement |
20	| `backend/` | The Python server. `domain/` is the pure core — the rules of the map and the arithmetic that works a change through it, no network, no model, no clock — and it is property-tested against maps nobody wrote by hand. `engine/` builds a world from a map, a branch and a seed; `api/` serves it |
21	| `frontend/` | The browser app: the canvas that draws a map, the wires, the Inspector, the two-world overlay and the keyboard. It reads the stored example today and is not joined to the engine yet. `src/api/schema.ts` is generated from the server's own description of itself and is never edited by hand; `e2e/` holds the one end-to-end test |
22	
23	## Working agreements (interview, 2026-09-16)
24	
25	* **ADR-gated cadence.** An agent drafts the ADR and spec first; Kent accepts, rejects, or amends; only then is code written. Nothing is implemented against a `proposed` ADR. Decisions Kent has already taken are listed in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §3 — do not re-litigate them.
26	* **Disgust veto.** Two conditions end a line of work immediately: a template-looking UI, and any state that cannot be traced to an input, a rule, or a cited source.
27	* **Vocabulary is the interface.** Use `spec/vocabulary.md` words exactly in docs, code, and UI copy.
28	* **Every number can say why.** Beliefs carry owner, interval, and provenance; two significant figures; model, user, and market beliefs are never merged.
29	* **Stacks tell the story.** One stack per spec; the bottom PR is docs-only; branch names are `<type>/<NN>-<slug>` with `NN` the stack number from the PRD roadmap. Conventional commits with `spec:` and `adr:` types in addition to the usual.
30	* **ARCHITECTURE.md is living.** A pull request that changes a boundary, layer, data flow, or runtime dependency updates it in the same PR.
31	* **Research reports are inputs.** Where a report and an ADR disagree, the ADR wins; where an ADR and the PRD disagree, fix the drift in the same PR.
32	
33	RULES FOR THIS REPO
34	
35	* Significant architectural decisions should be recorded at ./docs/adr in a numbered order. Higher number records supersede lower numbered ones.
36	* Enduring context between agents should live as all caps docs in the root of the repo, e.g. AGENTS.md, ASSIGNMENT.md, PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md. These should always be kept up to date if you notice them drifting.
37	* More detailed descriptions, diagrams about particular systems or complex features should be written to ./spec
38	* Specs should follow best practices regarding spec-driven development. Some key aspects of specs for this repo should include invariants and anti-patterns
39	* This is an experimental prototype and I am a solo developer. However, I would like to use best practices regarding commit messages, PRs, and PR stacks to maintain the navigability, hygiene, and legibility of this repo.
40	* Docs should avoid jargon, reference to other docs, or unexplained abbreviations and symbols. They should be self-contained as much as possible. That is, explain in doc what the concepts being referenced are. This also extends to doc strings and comments in the code.
41	* Be concise, punchy, and succinct without sacrificing clarity. Use formatting as a communication and legibility aid.

This is a take home coding assignment for https://catalyst.app/.

Catalyst is the agent layer for finance. We turn natural language — a thesis, strategy, hedge, or trading idea — into live execution across any market, venue, or asset class from prediction markets to commodities to tokens to private markets. It is a seed stage company with investments from Sequoia, Jump Trading, and Lux Capital.

Here are more details about Catalyst: https://coastalhq.co/scoop/e3a34548-1964-4b30-96ea-52801a558dd2

The goal of the project is to create a functional protoype of the concept behind Catalyst as a company. The full brief I was provided for this is located at ./ASSIGNMENT.md

## Map

| Where | What |
|-------|------|
| `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` | The compressed seed: decisions, requirements, invariants, anti-patterns, roadmap as PR stacks |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md` | The technical counterpart: layers, data flow, where each invariant is enforced, runtime, testing. Living; marks each section built or planned |
| `docs/adr/` | Numbered decision records (MADR format: context, options, decision, consequences); `template.md`; `README.md` index. Higher number supersedes |
| `spec/` | The spec as a book: one directory per idea (`graph/`, `multiverse/`, `thesis/`, `generation/`, `workbench/`, `probes/`), each with a landing page; `vocabulary.md` is the shared language |
| `docs/research/` | Four independent research reports (2026-09-16) that fed the PRD; inputs, not decisions |
| `plans/` | **Local only, git-ignored.** Agent-to-agent handoffs, working notes, orchestration. Start at `plans/README.md`. Nothing here is a source of truth — anything durable moves into a root document, a decision record, or the spec |
| `docs/initial-brainstorming.md` | Kent's raw notes; the origin of trigger/sustain links and refinement |
| `backend/` | The Python server. `domain/` is the pure core — the rules of the map and the arithmetic that works a change through it, no network, no model, no clock — and it is property-tested against maps nobody wrote by hand. `engine/` builds a world from a map, a branch and a seed; `api/` serves it |
| `frontend/` | The browser app: the canvas that draws a map, the wires, the Inspector, the two-world overlay and the keyboard. It reads the stored example today and is not joined to the engine yet. `src/api/schema.ts` is generated from the server's own description of itself and is never edited by hand; `e2e/` holds the one end-to-end test |

## Working agreements (interview, 2026-09-16)

* **ADR-gated cadence.** An agent drafts the ADR and spec first; Kent accepts, rejects, or amends; only then is code written. Nothing is implemented against a `proposed` ADR. Decisions Kent has already taken are listed in `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §3 — do not re-litigate them.
* **Disgust veto.** Two conditions end a line of work immediately: a template-looking UI, and any state that cannot be traced to an input, a rule, or a cited source.
* **Vocabulary is the interface.** Use `spec/vocabulary.md` words exactly in docs, code, and UI copy.
* **Every number can say why.** Beliefs carry owner, interval, and provenance; two significant figures; model, user, and market beliefs are never merged.
* **Stacks tell the story.** One stack per spec; the bottom PR is docs-only; branch names are `<type>/<NN>-<slug>` with `NN` the stack number from the PRD roadmap. Conventional commits with `spec:` and `adr:` types in addition to the usual.
* **ARCHITECTURE.md is living.** A pull request that changes a boundary, layer, data flow, or runtime dependency updates it in the same PR.
* **Research reports are inputs.** Where a report and an ADR disagree, the ADR wins; where an ADR and the PRD disagree, fix the drift in the same PR.

RULES FOR THIS REPO

* Significant architectural decisions should be recorded at ./docs/adr in a numbered order. Higher number records supersede lower numbered ones.
* Enduring context between agents should live as all caps docs in the root of the repo, e.g. AGENTS.md, ASSIGNMENT.md, PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md. These should always be kept up to date if you notice them drifting.
* More detailed descriptions, diagrams about particular systems or complex features should be written to ./spec
* Specs should follow best practices regarding spec-driven development. Some key aspects of specs for this repo should include invariants and anti-patterns
* This is an experimental prototype and I am a solo developer. However, I would like to use best practices regarding commit messages, PRs, and PR stacks to maintain the navigability, hygiene, and legibility of this repo.
* Docs should avoid jargon, reference to other docs, or unexplained abbreviations and symbols. They should be self-contained as much as possible. That is, explain in doc what the concepts being referenced are. This also extends to doc strings and comments in the code.
* Be concise, punchy, and succinct without sacrificing clarity. Use formatting as a communication and legibility aid.

1	# Kent's decisions on stack 04's open questions — 2026-09-17
2	
3	Asked through the question tool after a read-only Opus design review of `stack-04-generation.md`. The coordinator re-ran the review's central measurement before asking (209 dead versions; 89.05% → 99.4%). **All of these are settled. Reopen nothing.** Every brief on stack 04 names this file by absolute path, next to the round-2 note.
4	
5	## The six questions
6	
7	| # | Topic | Decision (Kent, 2026-09-17) | Lands in |
8	|---|---|---|---|
9	| G1 | **Record 0015 — where a claim's starting number and range come from** | **The range the model states, labelled as stated.** Record 0015 says *not yet* to an ensemble and names the measurement that would justify one (stack 07, against the eval scorecard). **No `engine/ensemble.py`, no extra field, no "runs agree" on screen, no N answers in a recording.** Why: record 0014 defines `lo`/`hi` as the 10th and 90th percentiles of the likelihood itself; a spread across re-asks on one shared map and one cached prompt is a different quantity (how much one model wobbles), the runs are not independent, "trimmed mean" of three is just the middle value, and it would multiply the stack's model spend 4–5×. Whole-map reconciliation stays not built — `spec/multiverse/diff.md`'s anti-pattern *do not infer a difference by matching two maps* is the warrant. **FR-8 and PRD §13 are amended in the same pull request** to say the question changed | `docs/adr/0015-*.md` (accepted), `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` FR-8 + §13, `ARCHITECTURE.md` §10, `spec/generation/proposals.md` |
10	| G2 | **`diff.md` open question 7 — "This happened" puts nothing on the change list** | **Count only the versions that survived, each by how much it survived.** One rule: *read the direction with the same weights the number was read with.* Measured on Hormuz, seed 20261001, `Observe(B, true)`: 209 of 2 000 versions have no surviving world; they weigh nothing in the number and the band but each voted against the direction. 89.05% → 98.66% weighted (99.44% among survivors). About ten lines in `domain/diff.py` (`_agreement_on` takes the weights its two callers already hold). No latency cost; under the five other edits every weight is 1 so nothing else moves. **Worlds per version stays 8. The 90% bar is untouched.** A dated amendment to record 0014, not a new record | `docs/adr/0014` (dated amendment), `spec/multiverse/diff.md` (OQ7 closed), `domain/diff.py`, `test_an_observation_puts_a_row_on_the_rail` |
11	| G3 | **A claim with no causes moved only by reweighting** (observing C moves H `.356 → .365`; inside every version H's paired difference is exactly zero, so its same-direction share is zero by construction) | **Keep the diff states; say it in the Inspector:** *"this claim moved only because the observation made some versions count more."* The same shape as K4 — a fact about the reading lives in the Inspector, not in a new state. One branch in `_states`, one field on the diff's row for that claim, one sentence, one paragraph in `diff.md` | `domain/diff.py`, `spec/multiverse/diff.md`, `spec/workbench/inspector.md`, `Inspector.tsx` |
12	| G4 | **After the validator refuses a proposal** | **Up to three silent retries — the plan as written.** *(Kent chose this over the recommended "re-ask once, naming the violations".)* The next call is **not** told what was wrong; three refusals in a row on one frontier claim closes that claim. Every refusal is an event and is shown. **Record 0003 gets a dated amendment**: its "one targeted re-prompt naming those violations" becomes "up to three fresh proposals, none told why the last was refused" — violation text never enters a prompt, so a prompt can never steer the model toward *passing the validator* | `docs/adr/0003` (dated amendment), `spec/generation/proposals.md`, `engine/expand.py` |

#!/bin/bash
# land.sh <pr> <title> <message-file>
# GitHub restacks a child branch onto main by itself when its parent merges, so this only:
# checks the base is main and the branch sits on main, waits for the four checks, squash-merges via the async route.
set -euo pipefail
PR=$1; TITLE=$2; MSG=$3
cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst
for i in $(seq 1 12); do BASE=$(gh pr view $PR --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName); [ "$BASE" = "main" ] && break; sleep 5; done
[ "$BASE" = "main" ] || { echo "base is $BASE, not main"; exit 3; }
git fetch -q origin
HEAD_SHA=$(gh pr view $PR --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid)
git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main $HEAD_SHA || { echo "head $HEAD_SHA does not sit on main yet"; exit 5; }
echo "head ${HEAD_SHA:0:7} sits on main; waiting for checks…"
for i in $(seq 1 90); do
  out=$(gh pr checks $PR 2>&1 || true)
  if echo "$out" | grep -qw "fail"; then echo "CHECK FAILED:"; echo "$out"; exit 4; fi
  if ! echo "$out" | grep -qw "pending" && [ "$(echo "$out" | grep -cw pass)" -ge 4 ]; then break; fi
  sleep 10
done
gh pr checks $PR | awk '{print $1"="$2}' | tr '\n' ' '; echo
[ "$(gh pr view $PR --json headRefOid -q .headRefOid)" = "$HEAD_SHA" ] || { echo "head moved while waiting"; exit 6; }
R=$(gh api -X PUT repos/kgang/katalyst/pulls/$PR/merge-async -f merge_method=squash -f commit_title="$TITLE (#$PR)" -f commit_message="$(cat "$MSG")" -f sha=$HEAD_SHA)
UUID=$(echo "$R" | jq -r .details.uuid)
for i in $(seq 1 30); do r=$(gh api repos/kgang/katalyst/pulls/$PR/merge-async/$UUID); [ "$(echo "$r" | jq -r .status)" != "pending" ] && break; sleep 5; done
echo "$r" | jq -c .

1	# Stack 04 — generation (04a ∥ 04b)
2	
3	**Nothing is waiting on Kent. He answered everything on 2026-09-17** — six questions and eight small corrections, after a read-only design review. The answers are in **`plans/notes/2026-09-17-kent-decisions-stack-04.md`** (rows G1–G6 and S1–S8), they are binding, and this plan has been rewritten in place to match them. In one breath: **no ensemble** — the model's stated range, labelled (record 0015, G1); **"This happened" is fixed by counting only the versions that survived** (G2), and a claim moved only by reweighting says so in the Inspector (G3); **up to three silent retries after a refusal** (G4); **$500 for the stack, a $15 hard stop per run in code, and only the coordinator spends money** (G5); **Hormuz recorded early, all four once the prompt is frozen** (G6).
4	
5	---
6	
7	**Goal:** type any sentence and watch a real map build itself, one claim at a time, with evidence — and with no key, watch the same thing play from a recording. After this stack the four example hypotheses from `ASSIGNMENT.md` all open, the numbers on screen are the engine's, and every proposal the validator refused is visible on the way past.
8	
9	**What this stack must not do.** No thesis card, no stop-loss, no tail strip, no live market prices (stack 05). No storage — nothing is kept between requests except what a running process holds in memory; the SQLite file is stack 05's (FR-31). No `refine`, no probes, no feedback-arrow unrolling (stack 06). **No re-prompting for a whole map**, ever (anti-pattern 2). **The model never mints an identifier, never declares its own provenance, and never decides whether a map is legal** (anti-pattern 1, record 0003). No ensemble and no graph-to-graph reconciliation — record 0015 (Kent, G1). No pastcast (FR-30, stack 07).
10	
11	**Rests on:** record **0006** (the model boundary — the SDK, the model, structured output, one proposal per call, the web-search tool, the cached system prompt, refusals shown not hidden), **0008** (five testing layers; recorded responses; evals out of band), **0012** (replay mode, accepted 2026-09-17 — built here), **0003** (the model proposes, our code disposes), **0014** (what it defers to 04: the provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths, and the open question that became record 0015, accepted 2026-09-17), **0005** (link semantics), **0010** (grounding; mostly stack 05, but FR-28's search at generation time is here). Read each record's "Decision Outcome" before writing a line.
12	
13	> ### Before any code that calls Claude, load the `claude-api` skill.
14	> Model names, request shapes, parameter names and prices change, and memory is unreliable. **Record 0006 holds the verified specifics** — the client library, the model name, the structured-output call, the thinking setting, the server-side web-search tool name, the cache-control block, the refusal stop reason. **Verify every one of them against the skill before typing it**, and put the price table in exactly one module with the date it was read beside it. This plan deliberately contains no model name, no parameter and no dollar figure. Every agent's brief carries this paragraph.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## How 04a and 04b stay out of each other's way
19	
20	Two stacks, in parallel, as 03a ∥ 03b ran. **04a is the browser; 04b is the server.** The split of every file that could collide:
21	
22	| File or tree | Owner this cycle | Rule |
23	|---|---|---|
24	| `frontend/src/**` except `api/schema.ts` | **04a** | 04b never edits a component, a hook or a stylesheet |
25	| `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` | **04b** | Only 04b runs `make types`, once, in its top pull request. A `schema.ts` diff on a 04a branch is a mistake to revert — **with one exception: 04a's bottom pull request, the engine fix (agent F), regenerates it for the one new field on a diff row** |
26	| `backend/**`, `evals/**`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.env.example` | **04b** | 04a never edits a Python file — **except agent F, in 04a's bottom pull request, which owns `domain/diff.py` and its tests for that pull request only** |
27	| `spec/workbench/**` | **04a** | Including the new `streaming-growth.md` |
28	| `spec/generation/**`, `docs/adr/**` | **04b** | |
29	| `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` | **04b**, in its top pull request only | 04b's agent writes the browser sentences from 04a's merged state, so **04a merges first** |
30	
31	**04a's first three pull requests merge first** (the fix, the chapter, the join). They need nothing from 04b to be correct, and they unblock Kent's eye on real computed numbers days before the model pipeline exists. **04a's last pull request — the growing canvas — is held until 04b's stream pull request is on `main`** (S6): its browser test plays a recording through a route 04b owns, **Add a claim** calls 04b's `POST /api/generate/insert`, and the `e2e` job runs every spec, so merging it early turns `main` red. When 04b's top pull request is ready, rebase its branch onto the finished `main` rather than merging `main` into it — a linear child restacks itself (STATUS, 2026-09-17).
32	
33	**The one true dependency:** 04a's third pull request draws a map as it streams, and the stream is 04b's. It is handled three ways and no other. (i) **The event vocabulary is settled in this plan**, below, and pasted into both stacks' briefs — the shapes-sheet trick from stack 02. (ii) 04a types the events by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`, exactly as stack 03b hand-typed `WorldView`; 04b's top pull request regenerates `schema.ts` and adds a **type-level test** that fails if the two drift. (iii) The 04a growth agent is launched in wave 2, after 04b's stream route is green on its branch, and develops against a server run out of the 04b worktree — read-only, no edits, no shared files.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## The pull requests
38	
39	### Stack 04a — the join and the growing canvas
40	
41	| # | Branch → base | Contents |
42	|---|---------------|----------|
43	| 0 | `fix/04-observe-direction` → `main` | **The engine fix both stacks stand on (G2, G3).** The dated amendment to record 0014; `spec/multiverse/diff.md` open question 7 closed and the reweighting paragraph added; `domain/diff.py` — the direction is read with the same weights the number was read with, and a diff row says when a claim moved only by reweighting; tests; regenerated `schema.ts` |

45	| 2 | `feat/04a-join` → #1 | `ApiWorldSource` switched on. Number slots fill; the fifth diff state `shifted`; the rail ranks; the computed chip sentence; the lazy conditional on a wire's midpoint; the six buttons move numbers; the retraction badge read off the world |

47	
48	### Stack 04b — the model pipeline, the stream, and the evidence it works
49	
50	| # | Branch → base | Contents |
51	|---|---------------|----------|
52	| 1 | `spec/04b-generation` → `main` | **Docs only.** `spec/generation/{proposals,grounding,streaming,replay,evaluation}.md`; the landing page's chapter table; **decision record 0015**, status `accepted` (Kent, 2026-09-17, G1); the dated amendment to record 0003 (G4); FR-8 and PRD §13 amended to match (S7) |
53	| 2 | `feat/04b-pipeline` → #1 | `engine/proposal.py`, `engine/prompt.py`, `engine/expand.py`, `engine/receipt.py`, `engine/pricing.py`. Stop rules, the Verify door, `no_path`, grounding, provenance written by us. The boundary cassettes |
54	| 3 | `feat/04b-stream` → #2 | `api/generate.py` — the event stream and two more routes. `engine/transcript.py`, `engine/replay.py`, `backend/recordings/*.jsonl`, `make record-demo`, the `recordings` job in continuous integration |
55	| 4 | `feat/04b-evals` → #3 | `evals/`, `make eval`. **No ensemble (G1).** The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths, **with the chapter sweep in the same pull request**. Regenerated `schema.ts`. `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` |
56	
57	---
58	
59	## The shapes sheet — the event vocabulary both stacks build against
60	
61	Settled here so two stacks cannot answer the same small question twice. **Eight events.** Each is one `event:` name with one JSON `data:` payload, in `backend/src/katalyst/engine/events.py`, mirrored by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`.
62	
63	```python
64	class GenerationStarted(BaseModel):     # event: generation_started
65	    generation_id: str                  # minted by engine/ids.py
66	    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with
67	    hypothesis: str                     # the sentence the user typed
68	    target: str | None                  # the Verify door's destination, in their words
69	    # mode, the recording date and the prompt hash are on Receipt and nowhere else (S3)
70	
71	class ProposalAccepted(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_accepted
72	    at: int                             # position in the transcript, from 0
73	    proposition: Proposition | None     # the new claim, identifier minted here
74	    links: tuple[Link, ...]             # its incoming arrows, identifiers minted here
75	    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open to expand
76	
77	class ProposalRejected(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_rejected
78	    at: int
79	    claim_in_words: str                 # what the model wrote. Never minted, never drawn as a tile
80	    violations: tuple[Violation, ...]   # domain/validity.py's own codes and sentences
81	    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open — BOTH growth events say it, so a claim closed
82	                                        # by its third refusal loses its skeleton at once (review, 2026-09-17)
83	
84	class BeliefsPropagated(BaseModel):     # event: beliefs_propagated
85	    world: World                        # the whole thing, from domain/propagate
86	
87	class Verdict(BaseModel):               # event: verdict — Verify door only
88	    kind: Literal["reached", "no_path"]
89	    path: tuple[PropositionId, ...]     # empty on no_path
90	    product: float | None               # the multiplied-out likelihood of that path (INV-8)
91	    nearest: PropositionId | None       # on no_path: the closest claim the map did reach

321	**Where a transcript lives before stack 05's SQLite** (*decided here*): in memory, keyed by generation identifier, for the life of the process, and streamed to the browser as it is produced. Nothing is written to disk except by `make record-demo`. Writing a second on-disk store now would be a store we have to migrate in stack 05 for no gain today.
322	
323	**The stream is a plain `StreamingResponse` generator (S5).** No `sse-starlette`: one fewer dependency, and no heartbeat comment line to land in a recording. The generator writes `event:` and `data:` lines itself, and stops calling the model when the client goes away — a test pins that. **`versions` and `worlds` get upper bounds on this route and on the three world routes (S2)**; today they are bounded below only.
324	
325	**Two things the chapter writers found, both in this pull request (coordinator, 2026-09-17).** (1) **`docker/nginx.conf` buffers the stream.** Its `/api/` block proxies with nginx's default buffering, which holds the body and delivers the growing map as spinner-then-dump — a veto, and only in the packaged build where nobody develops. Add `proxy_buffering off;` (and whatever else the stream needs — read nginx's own documentation, do not guess) to that location, and prove it: the `docker` job or a test must show the first event arriving before the last is written. (2) **`GET /api/readyz` reports what can be replayed.** Record 0012's on-screen sentence needs the recording's date *before* any run, and S3 put the date on `Receipt`, which arrives last. `Readiness` gains the list of replayable examples with each one's recording date, in the shape `replay.md` gives; `status` must not say `not_ready` for a program that can replay four examples. M owns `docker/nginx.conf` and `api/health.py` for this pull request.
326	
327	**Replay** (record 0012), in `engine/replay.py`: no key → the four examples play from `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl` through this same route (**Hormuz is recorded as soon as the pipeline runs; the other three once the prompt is frozen, at the end of this pull request — G6**), at a fixed cosmetic delay that an `instant` flag drops for tests. Beliefs are **not** replayed as numbers: the recording carries the seed and `domain/` re-propagates, so replay and live agree by construction (INV-5). Every recording carries **at least one `proposal_rejected`** and **one recorded intervention** — the scripted "…but Iran is struck the next day" its card offers. Any other insert is declined in plain words: *"drafting a new claim needs a model key."*
328	
329	`make record-demo` is the only way a recording is written, and a recording is remade whenever a prompt changes — the same checklist line the cassettes already carry. A sixth continuous-integration job, **`recordings`**, **passes on an empty folder** (so it is green from the commit that adds it), parses every file, checks each holds a refusal, and checks each prompt hash equals the current prompt's. No key in it.
330	
331	**Tests** — `backend/tests/api/test_generate.py` and `backend/tests/unit/test_replay.py`:
332	`test_generate_streams_events_in_order` · `test_the_stream_ends_with_done_or_failed` · `test_a_rejected_proposal_is_an_event_not_an_error` · `test_beliefs_arrive_once_after_the_map_is_built` · `test_generate_needs_no_key_in_replay_mode` (INV-13) · `test_replay_stream_matches_recording` · `test_replay_is_byte_identical_across_runs` (NFR-2) · `test_replay_is_labelled_in_receipt` · `test_intervention_on_replayed_world_needs_no_model` · `test_every_recording_shows_a_miss` · `test_every_recording_carries_the_current_prompt_hash` · `test_an_insert_is_validated_like_any_other_proposal`.
333	
334	---
335	
336	## 04b pull request 4 — evals and the spread (no ensemble — G1)
337	
338	**Evals** (record 0008, layer 3). `evals/cases/*.yaml` — the four `ASSIGNMENT.md` hypotheses, two Explore and two Verify, one of the Verify cases deliberately unreachable. `evals/run.py`; `make eval` replaces its placeholder and prints a scorecard; results to `evals/runs/<date>.tsv`. **Structure only, never wording:** no loops; at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` ending (INV-9); a rationale on every arrow and a source on every `documented` one (INV-2); resolution criteria on every claim (INV-1); a Verify case returns a graded path or an explicit `no_path` (FR-7); non-zero cache reads on a run's second call. Not in the build (they cost money and are not deterministic).
339	
340	**There is no ensemble (Kent, G1; record 0015).** No `engine/ensemble.py`, no run-to-run number, no *runs agree* on screen. One source-reading test keeps the door honest: `test_the_word_agreement_means_same_direction_and_nothing_else` — the only `agreement` field in the code is the diff's. **`evaluation.md` names the scorecard's fields now (S8)**, so stack 07 has a baseline to compare a critique pass or an ensemble against. **All four examples run once through `make eval` as soon as the pipeline is green (G6)** — structure only, no recording written — and the coordinator runs it.
341	
342	**The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths** — settled by Kent in record 0014 and deferred to here because every arrow on the Hormuz fixture is hand-written `argued` or `asserted`, so doing it in 03a would have widened everything equally and taught nobody anything. Now generation produces arrows that genuinely differ.
343	
344	```python
345	# domain/propagation.py
346	PROVENANCE_SPREAD: Mapping[str, float] = {
347	    "documented": 0.15, "historical": 0.15, "market_implied": 0.15,
348	    "argued": 0.40, "user": 0.40,
349	    "simulated": 0.50,
350	    "asserted": 0.60,
351	}
352	```
353	
354	Each of the 2 000 versions draws every arrow's strength from a normal centred on the stated strength with that standard deviation, **on the same log-odds scale the strength is written in**. "How well-backed is this" becomes "how wide is this" with no extra elicitation. **There is no `strength_lo` and no `strength_hi`, now or ever** — the spread is derived, never stored. The draw stream is **per arrow**, derived from the seed and a hash of the arrow's own identifier, exactly as the per-claim streams already are, so adding an arrow cannot shift another arrow's draws and version *k* of two worlds still shares its numbers.
355	
356	**Three consequences, and the third is the one that bites.** `test_band_is_not_sampling_noise` must now freeze **both** priors and spreads to get a zero-width band — it gains a parameter. `test_range_matches_analytic_first_order_on_fixture` needs the strength terms in its delta method. And **every quoted number in the spec goes stale**: the agent lists which chapter numbers moved and **the chapter sweep travels in this same pull request** — `spec/multiverse/propagation.md`, `spec/multiverse/diff.md`, `spec/graph/belief.md`, `spec/workbench/inspector.md`, `spec/workbench/tiles-ports-wires.md`, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` FR-21 and NFR-1. The roadmap's old "+8% on the fixture" was measured before the fixture was tuned; re-measure and quote the new number.
357	
358	New tests: `test_a_documented_arrow_gives_a_narrower_band_than_an_asserted_one` · `test_link_spread_comes_only_from_provenance` · `test_adding_an_arrow_does_not_move_another_arrows_draws`.
359	
360	**Four things this stack collected for this pull request (coordinator, 2026-09-21).**
361	1. **The path's multiplied-out likelihood moves into `domain/` and onto the world (INV-8).** Today `engine/verify.py::_multiplied_out` multiplies a path for the Verify door and nothing carries it for a stored or generated map, so the browser's path bar shows an honest absence (the browser must never multiply). One function in `domain/` beside `best_backed_routes` (the ONE route rule — K5), reading each claim at its own resolve-by day, a supposed claim counting as its stored `1.0` (the one surface allowed to read it); `World` carries, per claim, the best-backed route from the hypothesis and its product; `verify.py` uses the same function and its copy is deleted. `spec/multiverse/propagation.md`/`diff.md` and `spec/generation/proposals.md` B7 say so. The browser wiring (`pathProduct`) is a small follow-up on the browser side — list exactly what field to read.
362	2. **The diff row says WHICH half of the *unchanged* test failed.** A claim is `unchanged` when its move is under the floor OR its same-direction share is under the bar; the browser cannot know which, because neither constant is on the wire, so today its sentence says only that the engine does not say. Add one field to `ClaimDiff` (a plain word: `under_the_floor` / `versions_disagree`, nothing when the claim is not `unchanged`; the reweighting case keeps its own field) — `diff.md`, tests, regenerated types; list the browser file that should read it (`frontend/src/graph/diff/noChange.ts`).
363	3. **The payoff discriminator:** `ContractPayoff.kind` and `PricePayoff.kind` have defaults in `domain/proposition.py`, so they are absent from the schema's `required` and a model may omit the one field that tells the two payoff shapes apart (three real refusals in the first recording were `market_without_payoff` — check whether any was this). Drop the defaults; fix every construction site and fixture; the wire-schema test must show `kind` required on both. **This changes the answer shapes the model is sent → the prompt fingerprint → every committed recording and cassette goes stale.** So do it LAST, in its own commit, and tell the coordinator, who re-records (about $20 and three hours for the four). If the wire schema does NOT change (the SDK already marks it required), say so and nothing is re-recorded.
364	4. **`test_the_word_agreement_means_same_direction_and_nothing_else`** already exists (stream pull request). Keep it green.
365	
366	**Then:** `make types`, read the regenerated `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` end to end, add `frontend/src/stream/__tests__/eventsMatchSchema.test-d.ts` pinning 04a's hand-written events against it. Update `ARCHITECTURE.md` §1 (the event stream is real), §2 (the recorded loop-rejection test exists), §3 (all eight steps of a generation), §5 (INV-13's "still planned" column empties; INV-8's browser row), §7 (the boundary and evaluation layers become built; refresh the test counts, which say 137 and are wrong), §8 (`evals/`, `backend/recordings/`), §9 (record 0015), §10. And `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` §12's status row for stack 04 and §13's two answered questions.
367	
368	---
369	
370	## Pre-decisions — settle nothing twice
371	
372	Every brief on both stacks points at this table by absolute path. **Kent** marks something he has already settled, with where. *Decided here* marks a small tooling choice this plan took. **Open** marks the three things that need him before code — and nothing is built against them.
373	
374	| Topic | Decision |
375	|---|---|
376	| Two stacks | 04a (browser) ∥ 04b (server). 04a merges first. File split in the table above |
377	| One proposal per call | **Kent — record 0006.** Never a list in, never a list out. A 30-claim map is about 40 calls |
378	| The model never mints, never declares provenance | **Kent — records 0003 and 0006**, PRD §10 anti-pattern 1. The fields do not exist on a proposal |
379	| Provenance is decided by us | **Kent — S1.** A cited source **the search tool returned in that call** → `documented`; rationale only → `argued`; neither → `asserted`. `historical` and `market_implied` are stack 05's |
380	| Re-prompting | **Kent — PRD §10 anti-pattern 2.** Never for a whole map. `insert` is the single exception, over the affected subtree only |
381	| The request shapes | **Record 0006 holds them, verified.** Load the `claude-api` skill and check every one before typing it. No model name, parameter or price is written from memory |
382	| Prices | *Decided here.* One module, `engine/pricing.py`, with the day it was read in a comment |
383	| Transport | *Decided here.* `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`: the request has a body, and automatic reconnection would re-run a generation |
384	| Event vocabulary | *Decided here.* The eight events in the shapes sheet. A client ignores an event it does not know and says so |
385	| Naming before identifiers exist | *Decided here.* A proposal names an existing claim by the identifier the prompt gave it, and its own new claim not at all — one call returns one claim plus its incoming arrow, so there is nothing else to name |
386	| Caps | *Decided here*, plus **Kent — S2, G4, G5.** Depth 5 · width 3 · 30 claims · 3 refusals in a row closes a frontier claim (the retries are never told why) · 3 frontier claims at once · a searches-per-generation cap · a $15 spending cap per run · upper bounds on `versions` and `worlds`. All arguments |
387	| No ending reached | *Decided here.* One last ending-seeking call per open claim, then `done.reason = "no_terminal"` and an honest card. The engine never writes a claim the model did not propose |
388	| Verify and `no_path` | **Kent — FR-7.** A graded path or an honest `no_path` naming the nearest claim reached. No code path invents a bridge |
389	| Where a transcript lives | *Decided here.* In memory for the life of the process; on disk only through `make record-demo`. SQLite is stack 05 (FR-31) |
390	| Recording format | **Kent — record 0012.** `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, header line plus one event per line, every event of the live stream; `receipt` rebuilt on replay with zero dollars |
391	| Interventions in replay | **Kent — record 0012.** `do`, `observe`, `retune`, `believe` stay live arithmetic. Each recording carries one recorded `insert`; any other insert is plainly declined |
392	| Every recording shows a miss | **Kent — record 0012.** At least one `proposal_rejected` per file, checked in continuous integration |
393	| New dependencies | **Kent — S5.** One on the server — the vendor's client library — and none in the browser. The stream is a plain `StreamingResponse`. A second needs the coordinator's agreement |
394	| Recorded responses | **Kent — record 0008.** `pytest-recording` is already installed, `--record-mode=none` is already on, key-stripping is already in `backend/tests/conftest.py`. Only the recordings are missing |
395	| Evals | **Kent — record 0008.** Four cases, structure only, never wording; out of the build; `make eval` prints a scorecard |
396	| Cost receipt | **Kent — NFR-6.** Model, tokens, cache reads, dollars, per generation, on the `receipt` event and in the panel. Zero cache reads fails an eval |
397	| Provenance-derived spread | **Kent — record 0014.** The table above, as a standard deviation on the log-odds strength, per-arrow seed stream. **No `strength_lo`/`strength_hi`, ever** |
398	| The chapter sweep | **Lesson from stack 03.** An agent that changes a fixture or an engine rule lists which chapter numbers went stale, and the sweep travels in the same pull request |
399	| The word *agreement* | **Kent — K10 and G1.** The diff's column is headed *same direction*. There is **no** run-to-run number in this stack; the word stays free on screen for the day one exists |
400	| The likelihood slider | **Kent — FR-2.** A range with an explicit "I don't know" state; stored as a `user` belief; never overwritten |
401	| FR-9's critique pass | **Kent — S8:** **out of stack 04.** It is P1, it doubles the calls, and its value cannot be measured until the evals exist. Revisit in stack 07 with a scorecard to compare against. Tell Kent |
402	| Graph reconciliation across runs, and the ensemble | **Kent — G1, record 0015:** **neither is built.** The stated range ships, labelled. `diff.md`'s anti-pattern *do not infer a difference by matching two maps* is the warrant |
403	| Record 0015 | **Kent — G1.** Accepted: the stated range, labelled; not yet to an ensemble; FR-8 and PRD §13 amended |
404	| `diff.md` open question 7 | **Kent — G2, G3.** The direction is read with the number's own weights; a claim moved only by reweighting says so in the Inspector. 04a pull request 0 |
405	| Money | **Kent — G5.** $500 for the stack; a $15 hard stop per run, in code; the running total in `STATUS.md`; **only the coordinator spends** |
406	| When recordings are made | **Kent — G6.** Hormuz early; all four once the prompt is frozen; all four through the structure-only eval once, early |

# Stack 04 — generation (04a ∥ 04b)

**Nothing is waiting on Kent. He answered everything on 2026-09-17** — six questions and eight small corrections, after a read-only design review. The answers are in **`plans/notes/2026-09-17-kent-decisions-stack-04.md`** (rows G1–G6 and S1–S8), they are binding, and this plan has been rewritten in place to match them. In one breath: **no ensemble** — the model's stated range, labelled (record 0015, G1); **"This happened" is fixed by counting only the versions that survived** (G2), and a claim moved only by reweighting says so in the Inspector (G3); **up to three silent retries after a refusal** (G4); **$500 for the stack, a $15 hard stop per run in code, and only the coordinator spends money** (G5); **Hormuz recorded early, all four once the prompt is frozen** (G6).

---

**Goal:** type any sentence and watch a real map build itself, one claim at a time, with evidence — and with no key, watch the same thing play from a recording. After this stack the four example hypotheses from `ASSIGNMENT.md` all open, the numbers on screen are the engine's, and every proposal the validator refused is visible on the way past.

**What this stack must not do.** No thesis card, no stop-loss, no tail strip, no live market prices (stack 05). No storage — nothing is kept between requests except what a running process holds in memory; the SQLite file is stack 05's (FR-31). No `refine`, no probes, no feedback-arrow unrolling (stack 06). **No re-prompting for a whole map**, ever (anti-pattern 2). **The model never mints an identifier, never declares its own provenance, and never decides whether a map is legal** (anti-pattern 1, record 0003). No ensemble and no graph-to-graph reconciliation — record 0015 (Kent, G1). No pastcast (FR-30, stack 07).

**Rests on:** record **0006** (the model boundary — the SDK, the model, structured output, one proposal per call, the web-search tool, the cached system prompt, refusals shown not hidden), **0008** (five testing layers; recorded responses; evals out of band), **0012** (replay mode, accepted 2026-09-17 — built here), **0003** (the model proposes, our code disposes), **0014** (what it defers to 04: the provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths, and the open question that became record 0015, accepted 2026-09-17), **0005** (link semantics), **0010** (grounding; mostly stack 05, but FR-28's search at generation time is here). Read each record's "Decision Outcome" before writing a line.

> ### Before any code that calls Claude, load the `claude-api` skill.
> Model names, request shapes, parameter names and prices change, and memory is unreliable. **Record 0006 holds the verified specifics** — the client library, the model name, the structured-output call, the thinking setting, the server-side web-search tool name, the cache-control block, the refusal stop reason. **Verify every one of them against the skill before typing it**, and put the price table in exactly one module with the date it was read beside it. This plan deliberately contains no model name, no parameter and no dollar figure. Every agent's brief carries this paragraph.

---

## How 04a and 04b stay out of each other's way

Two stacks, in parallel, as 03a ∥ 03b ran. **04a is the browser; 04b is the server.** The split of every file that could collide:

| File or tree | Owner this cycle | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `frontend/src/**` except `api/schema.ts` | **04a** | 04b never edits a component, a hook or a stylesheet |
| `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` | **04b** | Only 04b runs `make types`, once, in its top pull request. A `schema.ts` diff on a 04a branch is a mistake to revert — **with one exception: 04a's bottom pull request, the engine fix (agent F), regenerates it for the one new field on a diff row** |
| `backend/**`, `evals/**`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.env.example` | **04b** | 04a never edits a Python file — **except agent F, in 04a's bottom pull request, which owns `domain/diff.py` and its tests for that pull request only** |
| `spec/workbench/**` | **04a** | Including the new `streaming-growth.md` |
| `spec/generation/**`, `docs/adr/**` | **04b** | |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` | **04b**, in its top pull request only | 04b's agent writes the browser sentences from 04a's merged state, so **04a merges first** |

**04a's first three pull requests merge first** (the fix, the chapter, the join). They need nothing from 04b to be correct, and they unblock Kent's eye on real computed numbers days before the model pipeline exists. **04a's last pull request — the growing canvas — is held until 04b's stream pull request is on `main`** (S6): its browser test plays a recording through a route 04b owns, **Add a claim** calls 04b's `POST /api/generate/insert`, and the `e2e` job runs every spec, so merging it early turns `main` red. When 04b's top pull request is ready, rebase its branch onto the finished `main` rather than merging `main` into it — a linear child restacks itself (STATUS, 2026-09-17).

**The one true dependency:** 04a's third pull request draws a map as it streams, and the stream is 04b's. It is handled three ways and no other. (i) **The event vocabulary is settled in this plan**, below, and pasted into both stacks' briefs — the shapes-sheet trick from stack 02. (ii) 04a types the events by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`, exactly as stack 03b hand-typed `WorldView`; 04b's top pull request regenerates `schema.ts` and adds a **type-level test** that fails if the two drift. (iii) The 04a growth agent is launched in wave 2, after 04b's stream route is green on its branch, and develops against a server run out of the 04b worktree — read-only, no edits, no shared files.

---

## The pull requests

### Stack 04a — the join and the growing canvas

| # | Branch → base | Contents |
|---|---------------|----------|
| 0 | `fix/04-observe-direction` → `main` | **The engine fix both stacks stand on (G2, G3).** The dated amendment to record 0014; `spec/multiverse/diff.md` open question 7 closed and the reweighting paragraph added; `domain/diff.py` — the direction is read with the same weights the number was read with, and a diff row says when a claim moved only by reweighting; tests; regenerated `schema.ts` |
| 1 | `spec/04a-streaming-growth` → #0 | **Docs only.** `spec/workbench/streaming-growth.md`; the chapter table in `spec/workbench/README.md`; close `diff-view.md` open question 1, `inspector.md` open questions 2 and 3, and `diff.md` open question 5 in place; the Inspector's reweighting sentence (G3) |
| 2 | `feat/04a-join` → #1 | `ApiWorldSource` switched on. Number slots fill; the fifth diff state `shifted`; the rail ranks; the computed chip sentence; the lazy conditional on a wire's midpoint; the six buttons move numbers; the retraction badge read off the world |
| 3 | `feat/04a-growth` → #2 | The stream reader; skeleton tiles; growth with pinned layout; wires in causal order; chips last; the input bar (hypothesis, Verify target, the likelihood slider with "I don't know"); the launchpad's three cards live; the receipt strip; the `no_path` card; the replay badge |

### Stack 04b — the model pipeline, the stream, and the evidence it works

| # | Branch → base | Contents |
|---|---------------|----------|
| 1 | `spec/04b-generation` → `main` | **Docs only.** `spec/generation/{proposals,grounding,streaming,replay,evaluation}.md`; the landing page's chapter table; **decision record 0015**, status `accepted` (Kent, 2026-09-17, G1); the dated amendment to record 0003 (G4); FR-8 and PRD §13 amended to match (S7) |
| 2 | `feat/04b-pipeline` → #1 | `engine/proposal.py`, `engine/prompt.py`, `engine/expand.py`, `engine/receipt.py`, `engine/pricing.py`. Stop rules, the Verify door, `no_path`, grounding, provenance written by us. The boundary cassettes |
| 3 | `feat/04b-stream` → #2 | `api/generate.py` — the event stream and two more routes. `engine/transcript.py`, `engine/replay.py`, `backend/recordings/*.jsonl`, `make record-demo`, the `recordings` job in continuous integration |
| 4 | `feat/04b-evals` → #3 | `evals/`, `make eval`. **No ensemble (G1).** The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths, **with the chapter sweep in the same pull request**. Regenerated `schema.ts`. `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` |

---

## The shapes sheet — the event vocabulary both stacks build against

Settled here so two stacks cannot answer the same small question twice. **Eight events.** Each is one `event:` name with one JSON `data:` payload, in `backend/src/katalyst/engine/events.py`, mirrored by hand in `frontend/src/stream/events.ts`.

```python
class GenerationStarted(BaseModel):     # event: generation_started
    generation_id: str                  # minted by engine/ids.py
    seed: int                           # what domain/ will propagate with
    hypothesis: str                     # the sentence the user typed
    target: str | None                  # the Verify door's destination, in their words
    # mode, the recording date and the prompt hash are on Receipt and nowhere else (S3)

class ProposalAccepted(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_accepted
    at: int                             # position in the transcript, from 0
    proposition: Proposition | None     # the new claim, identifier minted here
    links: tuple[Link, ...]             # its incoming arrows, identifiers minted here
    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open to expand

class ProposalRejected(BaseModel):      # event: proposal_rejected
    at: int
    claim_in_words: str                 # what the model wrote. Never minted, never drawn as a tile
    violations: tuple[Violation, ...]   # domain/validity.py's own codes and sentences
    frontier: tuple[PropositionId, ...] # claims still open — BOTH growth events say it, so a claim closed
                                        # by its third refusal loses its skeleton at once (review, 2026-09-17)

class BeliefsPropagated(BaseModel):     # event: beliefs_propagated
    world: World                        # the whole thing, from domain/propagate

class Verdict(BaseModel):               # event: verdict — Verify door only
    kind: Literal["reached", "no_path"]
    path: tuple[PropositionId, ...]     # empty on no_path
    product: float | None               # the multiplied-out likelihood of that path (INV-8)
    nearest: PropositionId | None       # on no_path: the closest claim the map did reach
    why: str                            # one plain sentence

class Receipt(BaseModel):               # event: receipt  (NFR-6)
    model: str
    calls: int
    input_tokens: int
    output_tokens: int
    cache_read_tokens: int
    searches: int                       # web searches this run made — billed apart from tokens, so
                                        # `dollars` cannot be re-derived without it (review, 2026-09-17)
    dollars: float
    seconds: float
    mode: Literal["live", "replay"]
    recording_date: date | None
    prompt_hash: str

class Done(BaseModel):                  # event: done
    reason: Literal["reached_terminal", "depth_cap", "width_cap", "claim_cap",
                    "spend_cap", "refusal_cap", "no_terminal"]
                                        # ONE RULE (proposals.md B4): the reason names what closed the LAST open claim —
                                        # an ending or a Stop -> reached_terminal; a cap -> that cap (three refusals in a
                                        # row is the refusal cap; it was "model_stopped", but the model did not stop);
                                        # spend_cap and no_terminal override
                                        # no "search_cap": reaching the search cap stops SEARCHING, not the
                                        # generation (later arrows are `argued`), so it is never a stop reason
                                        # why the GENERATION stopped. "no_path" is on Verdict only (S3)
    claims: int
    links: int
    rejected: int

class Failed(BaseModel):                # event: failed
    message: str                        # one plain sentence. Never a stack trace
```

**The transport is `POST /api/generate` read as a stream, not `EventSource`** (*decided here*). Two reasons, both hard: the request carries a hypothesis, an optional target, an optional user belief and a seed, and `EventSource` can only send a GET with no body; and `EventSource` reconnects by itself, which would silently re-run a generation and spend the money twice. The browser uses `fetch` and reads the body. The wire format is still server-sent events — `event:` and `data:` lines — so the format stays inspectable in a terminal with `curl`.

**Four things the cross-chapter review settled (2026-09-17), binding on both stacks.** (1) **A `Stop` and a closed claim make no event of their own.** A `Stop` leaves a transcript line; the next growth event's `frontier` no longer names that claim, and on `beliefs_propagated` **every skeleton goes** — the frontier is empty by definition — so no rectangle ever stands where nothing will arrive. (2) **Which recording plays:** the replayer matches the request's `hypothesis` against each recording's `generation_started.hypothesis`, exact after trimming surrounding spaces; nothing matches → one plain sentence, never a guess. (3) **Readiness says what can be replayed:** `Readiness.replayable: tuple[RecordingSummary, ...]`, `RecordingSummary{example: str, recording_date: date}` — one name, `recording_date`, everywhere. (4) **Anything that is not an accepted proposal counts toward the three in a row** — a validator rejection, a vendor refusal, a malformed answer — one rule, not three.

**A recording is this same stream, line for line** — `backend/recordings/<example>.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, in order, with a header line carrying the base map, the seed, the date and the prompt hash (record 0012). On replay every event is re-emitted unchanged **except two (S4)**: `receipt` is **rebuilt** with `mode: "replay"`, zero dollars, and the recording's date and hash; and `beliefs_propagated` is **recomputed** — the recording carries the seed, `domain/` re-propagates, and **a recording therefore holds no `World` at all**, which keeps the file small and makes replay and live agree by construction. Record 0012 names only four event types; the chapter must say all eight and say this.

## 04b pull request 2 — the pipeline

```python
# engine/proposal.py — what the model is allowed to return. One of three.
class ClaimProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["claim"]
    claim: str                       # the sentence, as a person would say it
    claim_kind: Literal["event", "market", "not_tradeable"]
    resolution: Resolution           # criteria, judge, resolve-by (INV-1)
    prior: Ranged                    # p, lo, hi. No owner field: we stamp "model"
    base_rate: BaseRate | None
    payoff: ContractPayoff | PricePayoff | None   # required when claim_kind == "market"
    not_tradeable_reason: str | None              # required when claim_kind == "not_tradeable"
    cause: str                       # the identifier of a claim ALREADY on the map
    link: LinkDraft                  # the arrow from that cause into this new claim

class LinkProposal(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["link"]
    source: str                      # both ends already on the map
    target: str
    link: LinkDraft

class Stop(BaseModel):
    kind: Literal["stop"]
    why: str                         # one sentence, shown in the transcript

class LinkDraft(BaseModel):
    mode: Literal["trigger", "sustain"]
    strength: float
    lag: int
    shape: Literal["impulse", "step", "ramp"]
    half_life: int | None
    rationale: str
    sources: tuple[SourceDraft, ...] # NO provenance field, and no identifier field

Proposal = Annotated[ClaimProposal | LinkProposal | Stop, Field(discriminator="kind")]
```

**Three things the model is structurally unable to do**, because the fields do not exist: mint an identifier, declare its own provenance, and return more than one thing. A new claim's identifier is minted by `engine/ids.py`; an existing claim is named by an identifier the prompt handed it; `owner="model"` is stamped by us; and **provenance is decided by us from what actually happened** — at least one cited source **that the search tool itself returned in that call** → `documented` (S1: a URL the model typed that the tool never returned is not a source, and is dropped with a note in the transcript); a rationale with no such source → `argued`; neither → `asserted`. `historical` and `market_implied` come from stack 05's adapters and never from a proposal.

```python
# engine/expand.py
def expand(graph: Graph, frontier: PropositionId, *, target: str | None) -> Outcome
```

One call, one proposal, then `domain.validate` on the map the proposal would leave behind. Accepted → mint, emit `proposal_accepted`. Rejected → emit `proposal_rejected` with **every** violation, and never repair. Both are events; both go in the transcript. **After a refusal the engine asks again for the same frontier claim, up to three times in a row, and the next call is never told what was wrong (Kent, G4)** — violation text never enters a prompt.

**The caps, all arguments with these defaults** (*decided here*): depth 5 layers · width 3 children per claim · 30 claims in total · 3 refusals in a row on one frontier claim closes that claim · 3 frontier claims expanded concurrently · **a cap on web searches per generation (S2; the agent picks the default and justifies it in `proposals.md`)** · **a spending cap per run, default $15 (G5)**. Record 0006 *estimates* a 30-claim map at about 40 calls; the first real measurement goes in `STATUS.md`.

**Two stop rules that are not caps.** A generation ends at `reached_terminal` when every open frontier claim has closed and the map has at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` ending (INV-9). If the caps are hit with no ending at all, the engine makes **one last call per open claim asking only for an ending** — and if that still fails, the stream ends `no_terminal` and the browser says so honestly. The engine never writes a claim the model did not propose.

**The Verify door.** The destination is added to the map up front as an ordinary claim; every call is told what it is; expansion is steered toward it. `no_path` is returned when the caps are hit and no path from the hypothesis reaches it, naming the nearest claim that was reached. **A bridge is never invented** — there is no code path that adds an arrow to make a path exist, and the eval case whose destination is unreachable proves it.

**Cost, and the hard stop (G5).** `engine/receipt.py` folds every call's usage into one `Receipt`, **and the pipeline checks the running receipt against the run's spending cap after every call**: over the cap, the generation ends `done.reason = "spend_cap"` with a plain sentence naming what was spent and what was got. The cap across runs ($500 for the stack) is a working agreement kept in `STATUS.md` — nothing is stored between runs until stack 05. **Only the coordinator runs a command that spends money; no sub-agent ever holds the key.** The pipeline agent builds against hand-written fake responses, adds `make record-cassettes`, and stops; the coordinator records. `engine/pricing.py` holds the price table and **nothing else**, with the day it was read and the `claude-api` skill named in a comment. A run whose cache reads stay at zero is a bug, not a slow day.

**Tests** — `backend/tests/boundary/test_expand_cassettes.py`, recordings in `backend/tests/cassettes/`, `@pytest.mark.vcr`, the suite already runs `--record-mode=none` so an unrecorded call fails rather than dialling out. **Every model call goes to one URL, so the recorder must match on the request body as well** (or the boundary tests run one call at a time) — otherwise two calls in flight are handed each other's answers:

**`insert` is the one intervention that calls the model** (anti-pattern 2's single exception: re-prompt only for `insert`, and only over the affected subtree). The other five stay pure arithmetic in `domain/`, so a reviewer with no key still gets the whole multiverse at full fidelity.

## 04b pull request 4 — evals and the spread (no ensemble — G1)

**Evals** (record 0008, layer 3). `evals/cases/*.yaml` — the four `ASSIGNMENT.md` hypotheses, two Explore and two Verify, one of the Verify cases deliberately unreachable. `evals/run.py`; `make eval` replaces its placeholder and prints a scorecard; results to `evals/runs/<date>.tsv`. **Structure only, never wording:** no loops; at least one `market` or `not_tradeable` ending (INV-9); a rationale on every arrow and a source on every `documented` one (INV-2); resolution criteria on every claim (INV-1); a Verify case returns a graded path or an explicit `no_path` (FR-7); non-zero cache reads on a run's second call. Not in the build (they cost money and are not deterministic).

**There is no ensemble (Kent, G1; record 0015).** No `engine/ensemble.py`, no run-to-run number, no *runs agree* on screen. One source-reading test keeps the door honest: `test_the_word_agreement_means_same_direction_and_nothing_else` — the only `agreement` field in the code is the diff's. **`evaluation.md` names the scorecard's fields now (S8)**, so stack 07 has a baseline to compare a critique pass or an ensemble against. **All four examples run once through `make eval` as soon as the pipeline is green (G6)** — structure only, no recording written — and the coordinator runs it.

**The provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths** — settled by Kent in record 0014 and deferred to here because every arrow on the Hormuz fixture is hand-written `argued` or `asserted`, so doing it in 03a would have widened everything equally and taught nobody anything. Now generation produces arrows that genuinely differ.

```python
# domain/propagation.py
PROVENANCE_SPREAD: Mapping[str, float] = {
    "documented": 0.15, "historical": 0.15, "market_implied": 0.15,
    "argued": 0.40, "user": 0.40,
    "simulated": 0.50,
    "asserted": 0.60,
}
```

Each of the 2 000 versions draws every arrow's strength from a normal centred on the stated strength with that standard deviation, **on the same log-odds scale the strength is written in**. "How well-backed is this" becomes "how wide is this" with no extra elicitation. **There is no `strength_lo` and no `strength_hi`, now or ever** — the spread is derived, never stored. The draw stream is **per arrow**, derived from the seed and a hash of the arrow's own identifier, exactly as the per-claim streams already are, so adding an arrow cannot shift another arrow's draws and version *k* of two worlds still shares its numbers.

**Three consequences, and the third is the one that bites.** `test_band_is_not_sampling_noise` must now freeze **both** priors and spreads to get a zero-width band — it gains a parameter. `test_range_matches_analytic_first_order_on_fixture` needs the strength terms in its delta method. And **every quoted number in the spec goes stale**: the agent lists which chapter numbers moved and **the chapter sweep travels in this same pull request** — `spec/multiverse/propagation.md`, `spec/multiverse/diff.md`, `spec/graph/belief.md`, `spec/workbench/inspector.md`, `spec/workbench/tiles-ports-wires.md`, `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` FR-21 and NFR-1. The roadmap's old "+8% on the fixture" was measured before the fixture was tuned; re-measure and quote the new number.

New tests: `test_a_documented_arrow_gives_a_narrower_band_than_an_asserted_one` · `test_link_spread_comes_only_from_provenance` · `test_adding_an_arrow_does_not_move_another_arrows_draws`.

**Four things this stack collected for this pull request (coordinator, 2026-09-21).**
1. **The path's multiplied-out likelihood moves into `domain/` and onto the world (INV-8).** Today `engine/verify.py::_multiplied_out` multiplies a path for the Verify door and nothing carries it for a stored or generated map, so the browser's path bar shows an honest absence (the browser must never multiply). One function in `domain/` beside `best_backed_routes` (the ONE route rule — K5), reading each claim at its own resolve-by day, a supposed claim counting as its stored `1.0` (the one surface allowed to read it); `World` carries, per claim, the best-backed route from the hypothesis and its product; `verify.py` uses the same function and its copy is deleted. `spec/multiverse/propagation.md`/`diff.md` and `spec/generation/proposals.md` B7 say so. The browser wiring (`pathProduct`) is a small follow-up on the browser side — list exactly what field to read.
2. **The diff row says WHICH half of the *unchanged* test failed.** A claim is `unchanged` when its move is under the floor OR its same-direction share is under the bar; the browser cannot know which, because neither constant is on the wire, so today its sentence says only that the engine does not say. Add one field to `ClaimDiff` (a plain word: `under_the_floor` / `versions_disagree`, nothing when the claim is not `unchanged`; the reweighting case keeps its own field) — `diff.md`, tests, regenerated types; list the browser file that should read it (`frontend/src/graph/diff/noChange.ts`).
3. **The payoff discriminator:** `ContractPayoff.kind` and `PricePayoff.kind` have defaults in `domain/proposition.py`, so they are absent from the schema's `required` and a model may omit the one field that tells the two payoff shapes apart (three real refusals in the first recording were `market_without_payoff` — check whether any was this). Drop the defaults; fix every construction site and fixture; the wire-schema test must show `kind` required on both. **This changes the answer shapes the model is sent → the prompt fingerprint → every committed recording and cassette goes stale.** So do it LAST, in its own commit, and tell the coordinator, who re-records (about $20 and three hours for the four). If the wire schema does NOT change (the SDK already marks it required), say so and nothing is re-recorded.
4. **`test_the_word_agreement_means_same_direction_and_nothing_else`** already exists (stream pull request). Keep it green.

**Then:** `make types`, read the regenerated `frontend/src/api/schema.ts` end to end, add `frontend/src/stream/__tests__/eventsMatchSchema.test-d.ts` pinning 04a's hand-written events against it. Update `ARCHITECTURE.md` §1 (the event stream is real), §2 (the recorded loop-rejection test exists), §3 (all eight steps of a generation), §5 (INV-13's "still planned" column empties; INV-8's browser row), §7 (the boundary and evaluation layers become built; refresh the test counts, which say 137 and are wrong), §8 (`evals/`, `backend/recordings/`), §9 (record 0015), §10. #!/bin/bash
# heavy.sh <label> -- <command...>
#
# The one queue for anything heavy on this machine: a whole test suite, a browser
# run, a repeat bar. It waits its turn, runs the command, and gives the turn back.
# One at a time, whoever asks. Last session three or four suites ran together, the
# load sat at 20-23, and the load itself caused "flaky" failures that then had to
# be chased (STATUS 2026-09-21).
#
# The turn is a directory (making one is atomic). It holds the owner's process id,
# so a turn left behind by a killed run is taken back rather than waited on for ever.
#
# NOT for a single test file, a linter or a type check: run those directly.
set -uo pipefail
LOCK=/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/.heavy.lock
LOG=/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/.heavy.log
LABEL=${1:?usage: heavy.sh <label> -- <command...>}; shift
[ "${1:-}" = "--" ] && shift
waited=0
until mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  owner=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$owner" ] && ! kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "heavy: taking back a turn left by dead process $owner ($(cat "$LOCK/label" 2>/dev/null))" >&2
    rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
  fi
  [ $((waited % 60)) -eq 0 ] && echo "heavy: '$LABEL' waiting behind '$(cat "$LOCK/label" 2>/dev/null)' (${waited}s)" >&2
  sleep 5; waited=$((waited + 5))
done
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid"; echo "$LABEL" > "$LOCK/label"
trap 'rm -rf "$LOCK"' EXIT
start=$(date +%s)
echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') START $LABEL (waited ${waited}s, load $(sysctl -n vm.loadavg | awk '{print $2}'))" >> "$LOG"
"$@"; code=$?
echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') END   $LABEL exit=$code took=$(( $(date +%s) - start ))s" >> "$LOG"
exit $code

- Never edit a source file under somebody else's running server; never trust an end-to-end number from shared ports.

I've read the four docs plus `AGENTS.md`, the stack-04 plan, Kent's decisions note (G1–G13, S1–S8), the shared agent brief and `land.sh`, and checked the repo against them. It matches the resume note. `main` is `48eb562`, no pull requests are open, the four worktrees are clean, and nothing was left running.

Five Opus agents are now running, and one browser repeat bar is in flight. Nothing has merged yet and no money has been spent this session.

## What remains of stack 04

Ten pull requests are merged. Four local branches are left, then a short tail.

| # | Branch | State | What's left |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fix/04-vanishing-wire` | Fixed, root cause shown | Its last bar (40× at 1, 3 and 6 workers), an independent review, the pull request, then land. |
| 2 | `feat/04a-growth` (the growing-map screen) | Reviewed twice | Rebase, then 20 cold runs on a quiet machine with the log kept. Two earlier failures are still unexplained. Then the pull request and land. |
| 3 | `feat/04b-evals` | Evals done, spread engine done | The spread's chapter sweep. The path product moved into `domain/` and onto the world. A diff row that says which half of "unchanged" failed. The final `ARCHITECTURE.md`/PRD/README sweep. The payoff `kind` defaults (item 6). An independent review, then `make eval` run by me. |
| 4 | `feat/04b-recordings` | Hormuz recorded | Record `midterms`, `export-controls` and `photonics`. This was held until item 6 was settled. |

The tail is the browser wiring for `pathProduct` and the which-half field, then milestone M4 where you look at a live and a replayed map, then close-out.

## Item 6 is now its own pull request, first

Item 6 is dropping the defaults on the payoff `kind` field. The open question was whether that moves the prompt fingerprint. I measured the shape as it goes out, with no key. `kind` is not in `required` on either payoff shape, so the fingerprint will move, and the Hormuz recording and the cassettes go stale.

So I pulled item 6 off the evals branch into a small pull request of its own, to land first. After it lands I re-record the cassettes (about $1) and then record all four examples at once.
